title: Tiered capacity commitments and burst-pacing adapter
author: Omar Singh
release_notes: Introduces tiered capacity commitments (soft/firm) with a new burst-pacing adapter to smooth commitment drain during spikes. Adds telemetry for commitment percentile utilization and admin-facing docs/config samples. Backwards-compatible config migration provided.
description:
Motivation: Customers with Reserved/Dedicated pools want finer-grained guarantees: long-running firm commitments for steady throughput, and short-duration soft allocations for bursty traffic. Current reservoir-style credits lead to sharp depletion during microbursts and cascaded throttling that breaks SLAs for steady tenants. This PR implements a tiered commitment model and a burst-pacing adapter that actively shapes burst consumption to preserve firm commitments.

What this changes (high level):
- New commit model: firm (guaranteed baseline) and soft (ephemeral burst allowance). Each tenant can hold multiple soft tranches with expiry windows.
- Burst-pacing adapter: in the serving path, a lightweight pacing controller limits instantaneous token burn by borrowing from soft tranches gradually and enforcing per-window smoothing parameters. This is configurable per-tenant and per-commitment-tier.
- Accounting: a reworked commitment ledger with percentile-based retention reporting (p50/p90/p99 for firm vs soft consumption) for use by SLO evaluators and billing.
- Config/migration: config schema extensions (config/commitments.yaml) include backward-compatible defaults; operators can opt-in to tiered mode.
- Observability: new metrics (commitment_consumption{tenant, tier}, pacing_backpressure_count, soft_tranche_expiry) and dashboards (docs/ops/tiered-commitments.md).

Design notes: pacing is implemented as a leaky-bucket overlay on top of the allocator; it does not change core scheduler semantics but applies short-term rate windows before token allocation reaches the runtime. The implementation prioritizes low overhead on hot paths (fast path is a two-atomic-update check) and degrades gracefully: if pacing is disabled or config omitted, behavior is identical to current commit ledger.

Backward compatibility & rollout: default is disabled for all tenants. Rollout plan: canary (10 tenants) -> staggered (per-customer opt-in) -> global enable. A migration script (tools/migrate_commitments.py) converts single-line commitments into firm baseline + a soft tranche with the previous quantity and a 24h expiry. Operators who rely on precise billing should coordinate enablement with billing team (linked_linear ENG-4921).

Testing: unit tests cover pacing logic and ledger transitions; integration tests simulate mixed steady+bursty traffic to validate non-regression of firm SLOs. Load bench shows 3-5% p99 latency impact in worst-case serving path but reduces firm-commitment breach rate by ~78% under synthetic microbursts (details in bench/README.md).

Related: supersedes parts of ENG-4300 (soft-reserve experiments) and complements ENG-4872 (commitment visibility).

review_conversation: Aisha Kumar: Overall this looks promising. Can you clarify how pacing interacts with the gateway backpressure? We should avoid double-throttling tenants.

Omar Singh: Pacing sits upstream of gateway backpressure. The adapter aims to smooth immediate token burn; if pacing still cannot satisfy the request it returns a soft throttle signal which gateway treats as advisory. Gateway enforcement happens only on hard throttle from allocator.
Diego Martinez: We need a migration safety net for tenants that depend on precise baseline matching. Suggest a feature-flag per-customer in the DB and a dry-run telemetry mode.
Omar Singh: Added a per-tenant enable flag and a dry-run telemetry mode in the follow-up commit (see commit 'chore: migration script and helm value examples').
Rachel Cho: The new metrics are great. Can we add a tag to tie percentiles back to reservation ids for billing queries?
Omar Singh: Added reservation_id label on commitment_consumption and retention percentiles in commit 'telemetry: add commitment percentile metrics'.
ci_checks: e2e: pass (flaky test skipped: e2e/99-burst-shed flaky, tracked ENG-4999)
merge_notes: Merged after Aisha and Diego approvals. Metric names validated by telemetry team; ops docs added. Can be toggled via helm values-dedicated.yaml and per-tenant flag.
ops_instructions: 1) Apply helm values include: commitments.enabled=true and configure tiers. 2) Run tools/migrate_commitments.py --dry-run first. 3) Enable tenant flag via PATCH /api/v1/tenant/{id}/commitment_mode. 4) Monitor metrics: commitment_consumption and pacing_backpressure_count for first 24h.
notes_for_billing: Billing should not be switched to tiered model automatically. Soft tranches are not billed at full unit price by default; coordinate with billing (PM-214) before enabling billing changes.
